title: Trace sampling budget enforcer and SDK middleware for cost-aware sampling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: As Redwood scales, sampling every request for full trace payloads is becoming untenable for high-throughput inference routes. We need a low-latency, cross-language mechanism to enforce per-tenant and per-route sampling budgets so we can retain representative traces while bounding trace ingestion/costs.

Goal: Implement a Trace Sampling Budget Enforcer and accompanying SDK middleware for Node/Python/Go that: 1) tracks and enforces sampling budgets (tokens/sec and burst) per-tenant and per-route, 2) tags requests with a compact sampling decision that propagates across services, 3) emits metrics for consumed budget and dropped-trace counts, and 4) gracefully falls back to probabilistic sampling when the budget controller is unavailable.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- Budget enforcer service (sidecar or centralized controller) accepts budget config via config API and exposes metrics: budget_available, budget_spent, traces_dropped, traces_forced.
- SDK middleware implements a constant-time decision path: check local token bucket -> attach compact decision header -> short-circuit to no-trace path with zero allocations for dropped traces.
- Propagation uses a 3-byte compact header format (version | decision | sampling-reason) to avoid inflating requests.
- End-to-end latency regression <= 1 ms p50 for common SDK paths when sampling disabled; < 3 ms when sampling enabled.
- Coverage: unit tests + interop test with gateway + canary rollout to dev and 10% prod traffic.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Centralized vs sidecar: centralized controller easier to reason about global budgets; sidecar reduces central point-of-failure but increases ops complexity. Plan: implement controller with local SDK token caches + lease refresh to reduce RPC frequency.
- Header format: prefer compact single header to avoid baggage inflation and extra serialization cost. Chosen layout: 1 byte version | 1 byte flags | 1 byte reason-code. This is intentionally minimal and allows future flags.
- Deterministic vs probabilistic drop: deterministic token-bucket gives predictable cost control; we retain a probabilistic fallback (stable sampling rate) when controller unreachable to avoid availability impact.
- SDK leak safety: middleware must ensure that when sampling decision is "drop" there are zero calls to expensive allocators (no span allocation), and minimal metric emission overhead.

Implementation plan:
1) Controller prototype: REST API to fetch bucket state and token refill policy, Prometheus metrics, storage in Redis for shared counters. (owner: Marcus)
2) SDK middleware: Node/Python/Go minimal alloc path + compact header encoder/decoder + local cache with soft-leasing. (owner: Priya Fernandez)
3) Gateway integration: gateway injects tenant/route context and honors controller decisions for upstream propagation. (owner: Platform GW team)
4) Observability: Grafana panels for budget_utilization, dropped_traces_rate, end-to-end trace latency distribution; alert when dropped_traces_rate > 5% for 1 minute. (owner: Observability)
5) Tests & rollout: integration tests (simulated high RPS), canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with kill-switch feature flag.

Open questions:
- Should the controller enforce quotas per-tenant per-hour or per-second by default? (Proposal: per-second tokens with configurable burst sized by route SLA).
- Persistence: Redis vs internal in-memory with periodic snapshots. Redis chosen for cross-replica safety.

Notes on compatibility:
- Backwards compatibility: if services do not understand the new compact header, gateway will map it to legacy tracing fields for critical internal services only.
- SDKs will expose an opt-in flag for "aggressive_low_memory_mode" which disables any trace allocation even for sampled traces (for extreme memory-constrained environments).

Rollout plan (detailed):
- Stage 0 (dev): controller + SDK instrumented on non-prod clusters, integration tests run nightly.
- Stage 1 (canary): enable on internal tenant + dev-product traffic (1%). Monitor budget metrics and traces_forced metric for anomalies.
- Stage 2 (prod gradual): 1% -> 10% -> 50% with 24h soak per step. Revert if traces_dropped spikes unexpectedly or SLOs degrade.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: Architecture reviewed with Observability and Gateway. Decision: centralized controller + SDK caching. Action: Marcus to spin up prototype controller image.
2026-03-04 - SDK design review: Priya presented Node/Python/Go middleware POC. Feedback: ensure no hidden allocations on drop; add microbenchmarks. (see PR #5142)
2026-03-06 - Tradeoff note: Using Redis increases deployment surface but required for cross-replica budget accounting. Ops requested TTL-based keys to avoid stale budgets.

2026-03-08 - PR opened for controller prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/5142. Initial metrics emitted: budget_available_total, budget_spent_total, traces_dropped_total.
2026-03-10 - Performance tests: local benchmark shows Node middleware p50 overhead 0.7ms when sampling enabled, 0.2ms when disabled. Memory impact negligible when using no-span path.
2026-03-11 - Security review: scoped. No PII added to header. Ops to confirm Redis auth and ACLs before prod deploy.
2026-03-12 - Next steps: complete Python and Go middleware, add interop test harness, prepare canary runbook and dashboard panels. Marcus assigned to coordinate canary with Platform GW team.
